concepts.name: Server-side caching
concepts.definition: Storing frequently accessed data on server (Redis, Memcache) to reduce expensive database queries. Server checks cache before querying database.
concepts.example: Check Redis cache for user data before querying database. If found, return immediately (cache hit). If miss, query database, return to user, store in cache. Reduces database load.

concepts.name: Cache eviction policies
concepts.definition: Rules determining which items to remove when cache is full. Common policies: LRU (least recently used), FIFO (first in first out), LFU (least frequently used).
concepts.example: LRU removes items not accessed recently. FIFO removes oldest items. LFU removes least-accessed items. Maintains cache efficiency and available space.

concepts.name: CDN (Content Delivery Network)
concepts.definition: Geographically distributed network of servers caching and serving static content (JS, CSS, images, videos) from locations nearest to users. Reduces latency and load on origin server.
concepts.example: Pull-based CDN: automatically caches on first request, ideal for frequently updated content. Push-based CDN: you upload to origin, CDN distributes, ideal for infrequently updated large files. User requests redirected to nearest server.

concepts.name: Forward proxy
concepts.definition: A proxy server that sits between clients and external servers, forwarding client requests while masking the client's IP address. The server sees requests coming from the proxy, not the original client. Used for controlling internet access, caching content, and anonymizing requests within internal networks.
concepts.example: Instagram proxies allow marketers to manage multiple accounts without triggering restrictions by appearing as different users from different locations.
concepts.analogy: A trusted friend who carries your mail to the post office so the recipient never sees your address — only your friend's address.

concepts.name: Reverse proxy
concepts.definition: A proxy server that sits in front of web servers and intercepts requests from clients before they reach the servers. It hides server identity, distributes load, and can handle encryption, compression, and caching. Clients interact only with the reverse proxy and may not know multiple servers exist behind it.
concepts.example: Nginx and HAProxy act as reverse proxies, distributing HTTP requests across backend servers. AWS Elastic Load Balancer and Azure Load Balancer are cloud-based reverse proxies.
concepts.analogy: A receptionist who stands between visitors and office workers, deciding which desk gets each visitor and shielding the workers from direct exposure.

concepts.name: Load balancer
concepts.definition: A system (hardware, software, or cloud-based) that distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server becomes overwhelmed. It increases application capacity and reliability by spreading requests effectively. Continuously health-checks servers to direct traffic only to responsive ones.
concepts.example: F5 Big-IP (hardware), HAProxy and Nginx (software), AWS Elastic Load Balancing, Azure Load Balancer, Google Cloud Load Balancer, and Vimeo Advanced Load Balancer (virtual/cloud).
concepts.analogy: A traffic dispatcher at a busy intersection who directs cars to less congested roads to prevent any single road from jamming.

concepts.name: Round robin
concepts.definition: The simplest load balancing algorithm that sequentially distributes requests across servers in rotating order. Each server in the pool gets exactly one request before the cycle repeats. When the last server is reached, the algorithm loops back to the first.
concepts.example: Four servers [A, B, C, D] receive requests 1, 2, 3, 4 as: A→B→C→D→A→B→C→D... The speaker notes this works best when all servers have identical capacity and load is evenly distributed.

concepts.name: Least connections
concepts.definition: A load balancing algorithm that directs each new request to the server with the fewest active connections. Ideal for handling longer-duration tasks or when server load is uneven. More adaptive than round robin because it responds to actual server state.
concepts.example: If Server A has 5 active connections, Server B has 12, and Server C has 3, the next request goes to Server C. Rebalances dynamically as connections complete.
